text: Good, ordinary day. Worked, cooked, called Mum. I wouldn't change anything.
Six months in the new flat and it finally feels like home. Plants on every sill, books on every shelf.
Life is pretty good right now. Not exciting. Just good.
Sunday roast with Owen and the kids, washing up together, film on the sofa. Content.
I like my job, I like my street, I like my little routine. Feeling settled in a nice way.
Finished the book I've been savouring all month. Satisfying ending. Made tea and just sat with it.
Retirement is suiting me. Garden, crosswords, lunch with Sheila on Wednesdays.
Simple pleasures: fresh sheets, clean kitchen, a good podcast.
Ate dinner on the balcony while the sun went down. Full belly, warm air, nowhere to be.
The garden's in full bloom and I made it this way with my own hands. Pleased with myself and the world.
No big news. Kids are healthy, bills are paid, Aziz made his good curry. That's a full life.
Satisfied with today's work. Wrote the chapter, edited it, closed the laptop at five.
Cosy evening. Soup, socks, the cat purring. I have everything I need.
Walked the same loop as always and still noticed new things. Life's good.
Our tenth anniversary. Takeaway on the floor of the living room like our first night here. Still happy with him.
Feeling at peace with where I am. Not the career I planned but a life I like.
Breakfast at the café with Phoebe, same table as always. Nice to have rituals.
Fridge full, house warm, everyone asleep. Good night.
Hosted dinner for the neighbours. Simple pasta, lots of wine, good company. Felt just right.
I'm okay. Really okay. Not just saying it.
Spent the day pottering about. Fixed the gate, baked scones, read the paper. Exactly what I wanted.
Got the balance right this week: work, rest, friends, exercise. Feels sustainable.
Watched the grandchildren play in the garden from the kitchen window. Couldn't ask for more.
Comfortable, pleasant, unremarkable day. The kind I used to take for granted.
Our little bookshop had a steady day. Regulars came in, Mr. Fischer bought his usual detective novel.
I don't need the big holiday this year. The garden and the library and long evenings are plenty.
Long chat with Imani over coffee. Caught up on everything. Left feeling full up, in a good way.
Finally finished decorating. Every room is how I want it. Walking around just enjoying it.
Pleasant day at the allotment. Dug potatoes, chatted to Arnold over the fence, came home muddy.
Satisfied. That's the word for this week.
Weekend at home with nothing planned and I'm perfectly happy with that.
Ate the first tomato from the garden standing in the sun. Salt in my pocket. Life is good.
I think I've finally found my people. Book club, the Thursday runners, Lin and Jae next door.
Mild contentment. Nice weather, steady work, good lunch.
Spent the evening mending clothes and listening to the radio. Small, useful, satisfying.
Our routine with the baby is finally working. Everyone sleeping, everyone fed. I feel settled.
Happy enough. A quiet life suits me.
Sat in the square with an ice cream while Tomasz did his shopping. People-watching, sunshine. Enough.
Everything in its place today. Inbox clear, house clean, dinner simmering. Lovely.
Glad I stayed in my hometown after all. Close to family, slow pace, the river.
Good meal, good friend, good chat. Mehmet always makes me feel at home.
Feeling satisfied with the year. Not perfect but solid.
Quiet shift at the library. Shelved books, helped a kid find dinosaur books, drank too much tea. Nice.
Pyjamas by 7, takeaway pizza, old sitcom. No regrets.
I like who I'm becoming. Slower, kinder, more patient. Pleased with that.
Afternoon tea with Granny Rose. She told the same three stories and I loved hearing them again.
The new job is fine. Nice people, fair pay, home by six. I'm content with fine.
Rainy afternoon spent baking with Lucas. Kitchen covered in flour. Very cosy.
Nothing to complain about today. Genuinely.
Paid off the credit card. Small dinner to celebrate. Feeling solid, settled, okay with things.
Spent the day fishing with Bao. Caught two. Let them go. A good day.
Our street party was lovely. Everyone brought a dish. Kids running about until dark.
Satisfied after a full day of gardening. Back aches but in a good way.
Feels like the right amount of everything lately. Not too busy, not too bored.
Morning coffee in the garden with Ilse. Birds, sunshine, the paper. I'm a lucky woman.
The house is quiet, the work's done. I'm happy to just be.
Long lunch with the old team. Easy laughter. Satisfying to see how everyone's doing well.
I've stopped wanting a bigger house. This one has everything we need.
Cooked a proper meal from scratch for the first time in weeks. Satisfying.
Content with the slow pace of village life. Post office, bakery, the pub quiz on Thursdays.
Pleased with the way the party went. Everyone seemed to enjoy themselves. Leftovers for days.
All the boxes ticked: workout done, vegetables eaten, called Gran, eight hours of sleep.
Watching the cricket with Dad, half asleep, the radio on low. Life doesn't get much better.
I've made peace with the ordinary. Turns out I quite like it.
Tidied, watered the plants, sorted the post. A small, satisfying Saturday.
Our little team shipped the update and nobody had to stay late. Pleased all round.
Feel comfortable in my own skin today. Doesn't happen often.
Shared a pot of tea with Mrs. Hale next door and heard all about her roses. Lovely hour.
Evening swim, fish and chips on the harbour wall. Summer done right.
It's been a good week. I've been present for most of it.
